content.value_statement: Long agent sessions can lose decisions, file history, and next steps during compression. This skill provides structured methods and probes that preserve operational context.
actual_capabilities: Compares anchored iterative, opaque, and regenerative compression methods.
Creates structured summaries for session intent, files, decisions, current state, and next steps.
Generates recall, artifact, continuation, and decision probes from conversation history.
Scores probe responses across six compression quality dimensions.
Tracks token efficiency through task completion and context re-fetching costs.
limitations: The included evaluator uses heuristic scoring instead of a live LLM judge.
Regex extraction can miss unusual file references, decisions, and task wording.
Opaque compression requires external implementation and separate fidelity testing.
Benchmark figures are source-specific and require validation for each workflow.

use_cases.title: Preserve Coding Session State
use_cases.description: Create durable summaries that retain changed files, technical decisions, test status, and immediate next actions.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers using long-running coding agents

use_cases.title: Evaluate Compression Quality
use_cases.description: Generate targeted probes and compare compression methods across accuracy, continuity, completeness, and artifact retention.

use_cases.title: Design Agent Handoffs
use_cases.description: Build readable handoff summaries that let another agent or person continue work without repeating exploration.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize This Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress this session into intent, files modified, decisions, current state, and next steps. Preserve exact paths and error messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner summary for a completed work segment

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Compression Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare anchored iterative, opaque, and regenerative compression for this session. Recommend one based on duration, artifact needs, and re-fetching cost.
prompt_templates.scenario: Selecting a strategy for an agent workflow

prompt_templates.title: Build Retention Probes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create recall, artifact, continuation, and decision probes for this history. Include expected answers and identify the context each probe tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Testing whether a compressed context retained essential information

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Compression Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this compression pipeline for cumulative loss, artifact drift, weak triggers, and probe blind spots. Propose measurable improvements and acceptance thresholds.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a production compression system

output_examples.input: Compress a debugging session involving an authentication failure and Redis connection changes.
output_examples.output: Session intent: resolve the authentication failure. Root cause: stale Redis connection. Files, test status, decisions, and next steps remain explicitly listed.

output_examples.input: Recommend a method for a long coding session where file tracking is critical.
output_examples.output: Use anchored iterative summarization. Merge only newly truncated history into stable sections and maintain a separate artifact index for complete file tracking.

output_examples.input: Evaluate whether a summary preserved enough context to continue.
output: Recall probe checks the original error and exact endpoint.
Artifact probe checks every modified file and its change.
Continuation probe checks the next test and unresolved work.
Decision probe checks the selected approach and rationale.

best_practices: Preserve file paths, identifiers, errors, and numeric values exactly.
Merge newly truncated content into stable sections instead of regenerating the full summary.
Measure re-fetching frequency and tokens per completed task.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize only for the smallest context on each request.
Do not compress tool schemas, API specifications, or essential function signatures.
Do not trust a compressed summary without probe-based validation against source material.

faq.question: Which compression method should I use first?
faq.answer: Use anchored iterative summarization for long coding sessions. It balances readability, artifact retention, and compression quality.

faq.question: Does this skill call an LLM API?
faq.answer: No. The included evaluator uses local heuristic scoring. Its API call is documentation for a production replacement.

faq.question: Can it track every file automatically?
faq.answer: Not reliably. Regex extraction can miss unusual wording, so critical workflows should maintain a separate artifact index.

faq.question: How should compression quality be measured?
faq.answer: Use targeted probes for recall, artifacts, continuation, and decisions. Track re-fetching and total tokens required to finish the task.

faq.question: When should opaque compression be used?
faq.answer: Use it for short sessions with low re-fetching costs and minimal need for human inspection.

faq.question: Can benchmark ratios be used as fixed targets?
faq.answer: No. Validate compression ratios and quality thresholds against your models, tasks, context limits, and operational requirements.
